The learner asks specifically: Make sure one of the senses is this meaning: to own or hold something.

notes: The possessor takes the oblique case before 'के पास' (or possessive pronouns like मेरे पास, तुम्हारे पास), while 'होना' agrees with the thing possessed.
Used for concrete or transferable possessions (money, a book, a car, time), not for family members, body parts, or illnesses.

draftBefore.shortGloss: to have; to possess; to be near
notes: Used with the oblique case of the possessor followed by the postposition 'के पास', paired with 'होना' to indicate possession.
Unlike languages where possession uses a verb meaning 'to have', Hindi uses this locative construction meaning 'to be near someone'.
